purpose: Pick how deep the independent review of a finished change goes. Never decides whether it merges.

change.diff: commit subject + `git show --stat` (first ~12 lines). Not the patch: the checkpoint was trained on states of ~384 tokens.

instructions.question: Which area does change.diff mainly touch?

criteria.data_deletion: Deletes, drops or truncates stored data, tables or columns
criteria.auth: Changes login, sessions, tokens or permission checks
criteria.money: Changes payments, billing, invoices or price calculation
criteria.breaking_interface: Removes or renames something callers use: an API field, endpoint, flag, export or event
criteria.refactor: Internal restructuring with no behaviour change
criteria.additive: Adds something new without changing or removing what exists

light-review.does: one fresh-context review on the fast model at low effort, then the normal merge flow

deep-review.does: fresh-context review on the reasoning model; the owner is named if it touches data or money

calibration.threshold_from: fixtures/merge-risk/tune.jsonl only: midpoint between the highest safe case (0.10) and the lowest risky case (0.16)
calibration.note: The top choice is wrong on 4 of 20 tune cases; the summed mass of the four risky areas is the signal. Re-derive the threshold on your own history before trusting it.
